items.descriptionAdvanced: The Koupe Massif is an imposing volcanic elevation, distinguished by its steep slopes and its striking presence in the Cameroonian landscape. The relief is a complex interplay of geological instability and tropical weathering, which has created a topographic structure known for its high botanical diversity. This mountain formation is also a central element of the volcanic line in western Cameroon and serves as a kind of natural guardian over the lower-lying regions. Geography K7 — mountains and volcanoes.

items.descriptionAdvanced: The Ntem Hills are a characteristic, rolling landscape form in southern Cameroon, defined by their gentle domes and the deeply incised valleys of the Ntem River. The relief is largely covered by primary, dense tropical rainforest, which embeds the gentle topographic structure into a uniform, green ecosystem. This undulating landscape represents a central part of the southern tableland, which reflects the geological stability and moist climate zone of Cameroon. Geography K6 — hill country.

items.descriptionAdvanced: The Dja Basin is an extensive, flat lowland structure in the southeast, which impresses with its enormous biological importance and its pronounced, water-rich topography. The relief is characterized by a barely perceptible topographic gradient and extensive swamp and rainforest areas, which form a natural protection basin for numerous animal species. This topographic unit is an essential component of the Cameroonian rainforest basin, whose flat and moist form significantly contributes to the stability of the entire regional climate. Geography K6 — lowlands.

items.descriptionAdvanced: The Kribi Coastal Plain is a narrow, topographically largely flat strip that forms the transition between the Cameroonian hinterland and the Atlantic Ocean. The relief is characterized by sandy soils, gentle rises into the inland, and a close intermeshing of marine- and terrestrial-influenced landscape elements. This coastal plain is not only of great historical importance for the coastal settlements, but as a topographic transition zone, it also offers a unique microclimate that harmoniously accompanies the transition from rainforest to ocean. Geography K6 — coastal geography.

items.descriptionAdvanced: The Bouba-Ndjidda Plateau presents itself as a hilly structured terrain within the Cameroonian savanna zone, the relief of which was significantly determined by the erosion processes of the local river system. The topographic form is characterized by gentle elevations and extensive, open areas, which are of central importance for the ecosystem of the northern savanna. This relief-rich, yet accessible terrain forms the landscape basis for one of the country's most important wildlife sanctuaries and shapes the open image of northern Cameroonian geography. Geography K6 — savanna geography.

items.descriptionAdvanced: The Waza Plain is an extensive, flat floodplain in the extreme north of Cameroon, whose relief is defined by seasonal changes in water levels. During the rainy season, this flat topographic surface turns into a vast wetland that attracts an enormous number of animals. The extremely flat nature of the relief is decisive for the spread of the waters and makes this plain an ecologically critical area that massively determines the annual dynamics of the northern Cameroonian landscape. Geography K6 — hydrography and wetlands.

items.descriptionAdvanced: The Logone Valley forms a fertile, low-lying alluvial plain along the border river Logone and is an essential component of northern Cameroonian hydrography. The relief is defined by an extremely low topographic gradient, which has led to the formation of extensive alluvial soils that favor intensive agricultural use. The topographic form is shaped significantly by annual flooding cycles, which constantly provide the soil with fresh nutrients and have thus created a highly productive agrarian relief in the north of the country. Geography K6 — alluvial landscape.

items.descriptionAdvanced: The Kadey Hills in eastern Cameroon are a topographically secluded, hilly rainforest region that impresses with its rolling relief and relative remoteness. The undulating relief is a result of the long-lasting erosive effect of the local river tributaries, which have created a complex, green-covered hill structure here. Due to its seclusion, this area is largely characterized by original vegetation, making it a significant retreat for the Cameroonian rainforest ecosystem. Geography K6 — hill country.

items.descriptionAdvanced: The Nyong Lowland extends as a moist, low-lying basin area along the Nyong River and is characterized by its flat, swampy relief. The topographic structure is closely tied to the Verlauf (course) of the river and exhibits numerous seasonal flooding areas, which form a characteristic, moist mosaic of forest and swamp biotopes. This flat, water-intensive nature of the relief significantly determines the ecological composition of the central Cameroonian lowland. Geography K6 — wetlands and lowlands.

items.descriptionAdvanced: The Sangha Depression is a deep-lying, extensive basin structure in the southeast, which, as a subsidence area of the Sangha river system, represents one of the moistest and least developed reliefs of Cameroon. The topographic form is characterized by an extremely low level above sea level, which leads to the formation of extensive, primary rainforest areas with high ecological complexity. As the deepest, continuous basin of the country, it functions as a geological and ecological anchor point for the moist climate zone. Geography K6 — basin landscape.
